answer: A per-identity capital stake makes a Sybil swarm self-defeating. Each key must post a bond before its answer counts, and the protocol slashes it when keys share one operator or reward source. To farm rewards an attacker must fund every fake identity separately and cannot reuse a slashed stake, so splitting a wallet into many keys only multiplies the entry price: once the bond exceeds expected payout, a thousand puppets cost more than the honest seat they imitate. The stake is timber in the gate, stopping cheap duplication, and no zephyr of mass signups can forge a real paid history.
